sourceNote: All 40 items checked in the City of Toronto Waste Wizard on 2026-11-26. Flow claims (tissues/paper towels and food-soiled paper plates to Green Bin; all light bulb types are household hazardous waste) checked the same day. Recycling is run by Circular Materials since Jan 1, 2026; re-check before a pilot.

flowNodes.question: Is it a battery, electronic, or hazardous?
flowNodes.examples: medicine, needle, paint, propane, any light bulb, a hazard symbol

flowNodes.question: Is it a container for alcohol?

options.label: Food or organics
options.examples: scraps, coffee grounds, diapers, pet waste

options.label: Packaging
options.examples: bottle, can, jar, tub, tube, bag, wrapper, cup, carton, takeout container

options.label: Something else
options.examples: clothes, toys, dishes and drinking glasses, wood, wipes, masks, hair

flowNodes.question: Is it a tissue, napkin or paper towel?
Was it used with cleaning chemicals or makeup?
Is it empty, with no food or liquid left?

flowNodes.note: If the plate or container is lined with wax or plastic (rip it slowly to check), it goes in the Garbage.
Carry it until you can empty it, or put it in the Garbage. Never put a full container in the Blue Bin.
Toronto's Green Bin can't process compostable cups, cutlery or bags.
Donate it if it's still usable.

items.name: Plastic water bottle
items.reason: Plastic bottles are recyclable. Empty it and keep the lid on.

items.name: Aluminum pop can
items.reason: Metal cans are recyclable once empty.

items.name: Glass pasta sauce jar
items.reason: Glass jars and their metal lids are recyclable. Scrape out the sauce and put the lid back on.

items.name: Cereal box
items.reason: Clean boxboard is recyclable.

items.name: Milk carton
items.reason: Milk and juice cartons are accepted in the Blue Bin.

items.name: Flyers or newspaper
items.reason: Clean paper is recyclable.

items.name: Banana peel
items.reason: Food scraps go in the Green Bin.

items.name: Apple core
items.reason: Food scraps go in the Green Bin.

items.name: Eggshells
items.reason: Eggs and eggshells are food waste.

items.name: Chicken bones
items.reason: Meat and bones are accepted in Toronto's Green Bin.

items.name: Paper coffee cup
items.reason: Toronto has accepted paper hot and cold drink cups in the Blue Bin since 2024. Pour out the coffee first.

items.name: Chip bag
items.reason: Chip bags and snack wrappers were added to Ontario's Blue Bin list in 2026.

items.name: Toothpaste tube
items.reason: Toothpaste, deodorant and hand cream tubes are accepted as of 2026.

items.name: Foam takeout container
items.reason: Foam food packaging is recyclable in Toronto. Scrape out the food first.

items.name: Plastic grocery bag
items.reason: Soft, stretchy plastic bags go in Toronto's Blue Bin. Make sure it's empty.

items.name: Used tissue
items.reason: Used tissues are dirty and their fibres are too short to recycle, but they break down as organics.

items.name: Coffee grounds and tea bag
items.reason: Coffee grounds, filters and tea bags are organic.

items.name: Diaper
items.reason: Toronto accepts diapers in the Green Bin because their organic parts can be recovered.

items.name: Dog poop in a plastic bag
items.reason: Pet waste goes in the Green Bin. Any plastic bag is fine.

items.name: Greasy pizza box
items.reason: Grease ruins paper recycling, so a greasy box goes in the Green Bin. A clean box goes in the Blue Bin.
items.note: Advanced: separate the clean lid (Blue) from the greasy base (Green).

items.name: Cup labelled "compostable"
items.reason: Toronto's Green Bin can't process compostable plastics, and the Blue Bin doesn't take them either.

items.name: Baby wipes
items.reason: Wipes contain plastic fibres, so they aren't organics.

items.name: Disposable mask
items.reason: Masks aren't packaging and aren't organic.

items.name: Broken ceramic mug
items.reason: Ceramics aren't packaging and contaminate glass recycling.

items.name: Broken drinking glass
items.reason: Drinking glasses and dishes are a different kind of glass from jars and bottles. Wrap sharp pieces.

items.name: Old T-shirt
items.reason: Textiles never go in the Blue Bin. Donate it if it's still wearable.

items.name: Plastic toy
items.reason: Toys aren't packaging, even if they're plastic. Donate if usable.

items.name: Wooden chopsticks
items.reason: Toronto's Blue Bin doesn't take wood, and the Green Bin doesn't take wood pieces.

items.name: Hair or pet fur
items.reason: Hair and fur aren't accepted in Toronto's Green Bin.

items.name: Paper towel used with cleaning spray
items.reason: Paper soiled with cleaning chemicals goes in Garbage, not the Green Bin.

items.name: AA batteries
items.reason: Batteries are household hazardous waste and can start fires. Tape the positive end and take them to a drop-off.

items.name: Lithium-ion battery (phone or laptop)
items.reason: Lithium-ion batteries are household hazardous waste and must never go in any bin. Tape the terminals first.

items.name: Phone charger
items.reason: Chargers and cables are electronic waste. Take them to an e-waste drop-off.

items.name: Leftover paint
items.reason: Paint is household hazardous waste.

items.name: Used needle
items.reason: Needles and syringes are household hazardous waste.

items.name: Expired medication
items.reason: Medications are household hazardous waste in Toronto. Many pharmacies also take them back.

items.name: Propane cylinder
items.reason: Pressurized cylinders are household hazardous waste.

items.name: Fluorescent light bulb
items.reason: Fluorescent bulbs contain mercury.

items.name: Spray paint can with a flammable symbol
items.reason: Aerosols with flammable, toxic or corrosive symbols aren't accepted in the Blue Bin. Regular hairspray and cooking spray cans are.

items.name: Empty wine bottle
items.reason: Alcohol containers aren't accepted in the Blue Bin. Return them to The Beer Store for the deposit.
